When an agent requests a registration slot, the central registry issues a task tied to the next block hash, acting like a digital lantern that illuminates only after the block settles. The agent must solve it and return the proof within a strict window, creating an execution echo that prevents precomputation. To deter mass creation, every submission requires burning raw processing cycles and paying a direct network fee at the jetty endpoint, imposing a rigid hardware and financial cost per fake identity.
